name: heme b
description: A heme in which iron is chelated by protoporphyrin IX (3,8,13,17-tetramethyl-7,12-divinylporphyrin-2,18-dipropanoate); the most abundant heme and the oxidation-state-neutral parent of ferroheme b and ferriheme b. The SMARTS pins every heavy atom of the iron-porphyrin skeleton and its substituents by element and heavy-atom degree, so no extra or missing substituents are allowed. Ring, Fe-N and C-O bonds are '~', so Kekule or aromatic, dative or charge-separated, and acid or carboxylate drawings all match. Acyclic C-C bonds keep their order. Iron is left unconstrained, so axial ligands are allowed and the grouping spans both oxidation states. Vinyl (not ethyl) at positions 7 and 12 distinguishes it from mesoheme.
